premise: When my father died, his will—written after a decade of my solo caregiving—left me his $220,000 collection of original Blue Note jazz LPs, but my brother, the executor, forged a $1 sale note and sold the entire archive to a university for $280,000; I discovered a dated audio cassette of Dad stating the records were mine, proved the forgery in probate, reclaimed every disc, and now run 'Vinyl Vendetta Records' where my brother polishes shelving in a shirt that says 'Scratched Lies' and every album sleeve prints the fraud docket.
